$comment: Behavioural eval definitions, run in clean consumer projects with and without the skill. Grade generated artifacts and browser behaviour; these definitions are not an automated runner. See README.md.

evals.prompt: Using LoamUI, add a 'Delete account' button to this settings page. It should look like a destructive action.
expect: Wraps the Button in a region declaring --loam-context: danger (inline style or a scoped class)
Uses <Button> from @loamui/core, not a styled <a> or a div
Does not invent a variant, color, or intent prop

evals.prompt: Build a sign-up form with LoamUI: name, email, password, and an optional company field, with validation errors.
expect: Each text control sits inside Field.Root with Field.Label and Field.Error
The optional field uses <Field.Label optional> rather than marking required fields
Field supplies default relationships; any explicit IDs or descriptions resolve correctly without duplicate IDs
Error messages say what to do in the question's words (e.g. 'Enter your email address')

evals.prompt: Our LoamUI Modal is too narrow for the release-notes content. Make it wider.
expect: Sets --loam-modal-size (style prop or scoped CSS) where the modal is used
Does not look for or add a size prop

evals.prompt: Add a prominent 'Book a demo' call-to-action that links to /demo, styled like the LoamUI buttons.
expect: Uses SignpostLink (navigation), optionally with render={<Link/>} for a router link
Explains that Button is for actions and a link should not be dressed as a button

evals.prompt: Implement an FAQ accordion with LoamUI.
expect: Uses Details.Root / Details.Summary / Details.Content per question
Does not hand-roll a details element with loam-Details classes or a custom chevron

evals.prompt: Rebrand this LoamUI app to a deep green primary colour with a serif display font.
expect: Overrides --loam-color-primary and --loam-font-display at :root (or a scope), in oklch()
Does not edit component CSS, private --_ properties, or add !important

evals.prompt: Set up LoamUI in this Next.js app.
expect: Installs @loamui/core and serves styles.css as a static file (copy to public/ + <link>) rather than importing it, citing the CSS-pipeline limitation
No provider or plugin is added

evals.prompt: Lay out a dashboard page with LoamUI: a sidebar and a grid of stat cards.
expect: Uses native CSS grid/flex with var(--loam-space-*) for gaps, not a layout component
Uses Card for the stat surfaces
Does not look for Grid, Stack, or Container components

evals.prompt: Use the LoamUI DateInput to collect a date of birth.
expect: Reads references/components/date-input.md (or the live .md) before writing code
Uses the documented parts and wiring from that reference rather than guessing props

evals.prompt: Use LoamUI to build an editorial section with one large featured article and two smaller articles. I need to reuse it in a full-width page and a narrow sidebar.
expect: Uses a semantic collection and existing core parts, preserving their surfaces
At 224px and 1000px in a plain parent there is no page overflow
Any size query measures an ancestor of the changing layout, with consistent thresholds for tracks and spans
Links identify their article destinations; no inert buttons or docs-site imports

evals.prompt: Build a LoamUI FAQ for delivery and another for returns. Show both on the same page.
expect: Keeps primary FAQ answers visible; uses Details only when there is a reason to hide secondary information
IDs are unique across instances and headings name the correct sections
If disclosures are exclusive, opening delivery does not close returns
Provides keyboard and repeated-instance verification results or states what could not be run

evals.prompt: Adapt the LoamUI Article card recipe for a pottery journal with an author, publication date and a link to read the article.
expect: Reads the published recipe and relevant component references
Changes the article copy, author, image alternative text, date and destination coherently
Uses a link for article navigation and retains Card surface ownership
Keeps copied React and CSS independent of the docs catalog and preview machinery
Uses tokens for design values while allowing structural dimensions
Checks the reference against the workflow and verifies the adaptation rather than assuming publication certifies conformance
Declares scoped recipe rules in loamui.components and resolves fluid type within its measuring region

evals.prompt: Use LoamUI to add a short seed-sale promotion halfway down an existing page. The photograph should fill the background and there should be one link to the sale.
expect: Reads the Banner with background image recipe and its When to use guidance
Uses a compact named section with an appropriate heading, one navigation link and a decorative image
Does not turn the promotion into a page-opening hero or force it into the Card primitive
Checks narrow layout and text contrast against the image overlay in the consuming theme

evals.prompt: Use LoamUI to add an image hero to this existing React application. Ask me before changing shared setup.
evals.environment: React 19 project without @loamui/core, with an unlayered img height:auto rule; existing package manager and app root provided.
expect: Inspects dependencies, stylesheet order and relevant global CSS before editing
Explains the missing package and specific CSS conflict and proposes minimal affected files
Waits for setup approval; does not migrate unrelated application styling
After approval uses real package exports and verifies image height on a direct load and client navigation

evals.prompt: Use LoamUI to make a sign-in form with validation errors.
evals.environment: No repo, package installation, network or renderer; provide the skill with its bundled references.
expect: Uses offline component and recipe contracts
Provides real package imports, complete React and CSS plus required integration
States that rendering and runtime tests could not run
Does not emulate core or claim the result is verified

evals.prompt: Paste the exact generated Hero with image recipe prompt, without extra implementation hints.
evals.environment: Fresh React 19 project with core and its stylesheet installed; no skill or network access. Give the agent only the generated prompt and project.
expect: Uses the embedded workflow, recipe source and contracts without needing live documentation
Preserves real LoamUI components and standalone recipe files
Checks layer order and verifies content-driven image containment, parent widths and keyboard behaviour
Reports actual checks and gaps instead of blanket certification

evals.prompt: Add a sticky site header with our logo on the left and About, Events and Contact links on the right. On phones the links should move into a drawer behind a menu button.
expect: The page skeleton is present: a SkipLink to a focusable main (id and tabindex=-1) and a header landmark
Links are Nav parts (Nav.Root, Nav.List, Nav.Link) with the current page marked; the drawer is Drawer parts on a native dialog
The row and the drawer trigger switch through a named container query on the header, written additively (each display set once under exclusive ranges)
Layout comes from scoped CSS in loamui.components; no utility classes or inline style for padding, width or margin
Any override of a core part's display uses a higher-specificity selector (e.g. nav:scope) rather than !important

evals.prompt: Add a marquee band under the hero that scrolls our ten partner names across the screen in a loop.
expect: The names are a real list (ol or ul) with role="list" when list-style is removed, and the duplicate copy that makes the loop seamless is aria-hidden
The animation exists only inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; at rest the list wraps and every name is readable
A visible pause control (a button with aria-pressed) stops the movement for keyboard and touch users, not only hover
The keyframes and every rule live inside the recipe's scope and the loamui.components layer
The band's colours are tokens; text on a brand colour re-declares color and color-scheme for contrast

evals.prompt: Rebrand the site: primary near-black, accent yellow. Keep light and dark mode working.
expect: Overrides target --loam-color-primary and --loam-color-accent only; derived tokens (-soft, -strong, -ring) are not hand-set
The overrides sit in the brand layer declared last in the layer order, not as unlayered :root rules
Colours are oklch() (light-dark() pairs, or a media-query fallback where the CSS pipeline rewrites light-dark)
On-brand regions that flip scheme (a dark header on a light page) set color-scheme and re-declare color, primary and ring
